output.answer: Detecting a poisoned document doesn't mean a RAG model resists it: work on reasoning over poisoned context reports that detection does not guarantee resistance. Models also show conformity bias, so when most retrieved documents endorse a poisoned claim they tend to go along with the majority. The number of poisoned documents matters in both directions: a majority of poisoned passages pushes the model toward the false claim, yet a single crafted document can be enough, and an attack can also be spread across many small, collaborating pieces.

output.answer: Not very reliable: misleading knowledge can induce deep research agents to reach false conclusions. They also commit prematurely to answers, a failure that one line of work predicts and repairs, and the first move of a deep search shapes the outcome. Benchmarks find that the hard part comes after search, when agents must synthesize and organize what they found, and error analyses of deep search and deep research agents catalog where they fail. Robustness to incomplete knowledge is a separate weakness, studied diagnostically for KG-based QA and KG-RAG.

output.answer: Adding agents doesn't always help: one study of multi-agent collaboration finds cases where more is less. Collectively, LLM multi-agent systems are vulnerable to herding and runaway cascades, and multi-agent search can show absorbing-state phase transitions. Partial observability is another setting with its own benchmark for multi-agent collaboration, and heterogeneous systems need not give every agent the strongest model.

output.answer: Tool-calling pipelines place implicit trust in tools, and that trust can be measured and exploited. On the permissions side, MCP servers can launder filesystem capabilities to expose credentials, and MCP lets resources be abused across domains. Adversarial context injected at different MCP layers affects model robustness, and agents in the MCP ecosystem can be hijacked through trace-optimized attacks. Proposed fixes include attested capability leases for execution-time trust and kill-chain-aligned detection of multi-step attacks.
